requirement:
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.

HTML comment blocks are excluded from structural hashes. Inline HTML comments
within paragraph text remain ordinary paragraph text. Paragraph and directive
prose uses word-based hashing. Reflowing whitespace within the same paragraph,
while preserving its words and surrounding outline structure, preserves the
hash. Changing its words changes the structural encoding.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover every obligation in `requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.fingerprints`. I found no gaps. The mapping is below.

- **SHA-256 over the word-based encoding.**
  - `bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries` asserts that the Markdown fingerprint is 64 hex digits.
  - The shared `Encoder` has a known-answer test, `hashes_include_grammar_kinds_nesting_and_sha256_digests` in `outline/tests.rs`. It checks the standard SHA-256 empty vector and a tagged, length-prefixed text token. I read this only as a search snippet, so I treat it as supporting evidence.
  - The Markdown-specific tests cannot check SHA-256 more directly, because the exact encoding is unspecified.
- **Fingerprint scheme.** `bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline` asserts that `languages::Markdown` reports `markdown-structural-v1` and that loaded contents retain it. The cited requirement `requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme` is context only.
- **HTML comment blocks are excluded.**
  - `comments_are_excluded_from_hashes_in_every_other_profile`, `a.md` case: changing a block comment's text or deleting it leaves the hash unchanged, and changing a non-comment word changes it.
  - `bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries` has the same comment-change case for Markdown.
  - `markdown_comments_are_html_comment_blocks_not_inline_comments` shows that only the block is recorded as a comment.
- **Inline HTML comments stay paragraph text.**
  - In `bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries`, changing `one` to `two` inside an inline `<!-- one -->` changes the hash.
  - `markdown_comments_are_html_comment_blocks_not_inline_comments` shows that the owner of the inline-comment line is a `paragraph` node.
- **Word-based hashing and reflow.**
  - `reflowing_markdown_paragraphs_keeps_the_hash`: reflowing keeps the hash, and `brownfox` differs from `brown fox`.
  - `prose_words_are_encoded_separately`: leading, trailing, and internal whitespace do not matter, and `ab cd` differs from `abcd`.
  - `markdown_hashes_include_paragraph_text_between_punctuation_tokens`: adding a word changes the hash, and extra spaces do not.
  - `anonymous_identities_survive_reflow_and_sibling_edits_and_number_duplicates`: reflowing a paragraph inside a nested directive keeps the hash, and changing the words changes it.
- **Directive prose.** `directive_prose_hashes_words_across_reflow_without_joining_them` compares directive fingerprints. Reflowed `two words` matches the original, and `twowords` differs.

Together these tests exercise each stated behavior (comments excluded, inline comments kept, word hashing, reflow-invariance) and assert both the unchanged and the changed outcomes. The `{test}` references to the subject are present.

text: :::{req} fingerprints
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.
HTML comment blocks are excluded from structural hashes. Inline HTML comments
within paragraph text remain ordinary paragraph text. Paragraph and directive
prose uses word-based hashing. Reflowing whitespace within the same paragraph,
while preserving its words and surrounding outline structure, preserves the
hash. Changing its words changes the structural encoding.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text and its
profile's comment group MUST be hashed, not its delimiter tokens such as `//`,
`///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`; the Rust profile's groups are inner
and outer doc comments. The words of consecutive included comments of one group
MUST be hashed as one ordered list, so reflowing them across more or fewer lines
or comments does not change the hash, while moving text between groups does. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
:::{req} language_provider.fingerprint_scheme
Each language supplies the scheme identifying its structural-hash rules and
their version. A change to those rules uses a different scheme; an update
preserving the calculation can retain the scheme. Loaded contents retain the
scheme used to compute their hashes.
```rust,ignore
pub trait OutlineLang: Clone + Send + Sync {
/// Identify the structural-hash rules and their version.
fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
impl OutlineContent {
/// The selected item's structural digest from this snapshot.
pub fn structural_hash(&self) -> &str;
/// The retained scheme identifying its hashing rules and version.
pub fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
